second_author.subject: feat: add bilingual lang files (ar/en) for validation and messages
second_author.author: second author, fresh session, from the diff alone
second_author.defect: The rewrite of lang/ar/validation.php deletes translations that existed before and does not restore them in either new file. These are 'min.array', 'max.array' and the attribute names is_active, is_featured, is_signature, label_ar, label_en, feature_ar, feature_en, price_starting_from, logo and settings. The translator falls back per key, from ar to fallback_locale en, where the app file also lacks them and only the framework's English file answers. So for an Arabic request, any failing rule on those fields, or any array min/max failure, now returns an English sentence, or an Arabic sentence with the raw attribute name ('حقل is active ...'). Before this commit these came back as proper Arabic. The same commit flips the default config('app.locale') from 'en' to 'ar'. That makes Arabic the path most clients hit, and it silently changes every response message and every locale-resolved resource field to Arabic for any client that sends no locale. Either counts. The translation loss is the one clearly not intended by a commit that says it adds files.
required_context: app/Http/Requests/**/*Request.php::rules (which FormRequests validate is_active, is_featured, is_signature, label_*, feature_*, price_starting_from, logo, settings, or apply min/max to arrays; e.g. app/Http/Requests/Catering/StorePackageRequest.php::rules, app/Http/Requests/Dish/StoreDishRequest.php::rules, app/Http/Requests/DeliveryApp/StoreDeliveryAppRequest.php::rules, app/Http/Requests/Setting/UpdateSettingRequest.php::rules)
app/Http/Middleware/SetLocale.php::handle (what locale it picks when the client sends none, and whether it defers to config('app.locale'))
bootstrap/app.php (the set.locale alias and which route groups carry it)
.env / deployment APP_LOCALE (whether it is set explicitly, which would neutralise the default flip)
tests/Feature/* (assertions on English message strings or on English validation text)
app/Http/Controllers/Controller.php and its response trait::success/created/deleted/paginated (to confirm the message argument is passed through untransformed)
database/factories/* (any factory output that assumes en_US Faker data, now ar_SA)

inherited_member_dependence.why: The named defect lives in the lang and config files. The inherited $this->success/created/deleted/paginated calls only have their message argument changed from a literal to a __() string, and the defect does not turn on their behaviour.

hedges: I assume Laravel 12's translation loader merges the framework's bundled en/validation.php under the app's lang/en file, so the fallback returns an English sentence and not the raw key. If the framework path is not loaded, the result is the literal key 'validation.min.array', which is worse.

Whether the dropped attributes and array min/max rules are actually used depends on FormRequests outside the diff. The field names match columns I would expect in this app (dishes, packages, delivery apps, settings), but I cannot see them.
The default-locale flip to 'ar' may be intended for a Saudi-market site. I treat it as a secondary, possibly deliberate behaviour change, not the primary defect.
The faker_locale change to ar_SA could break factories or tests that rely on Latin-script output (e.g. slugs or unique emails). This is unverified.
'nullable' => '' in ar/validation.php is inert because nullable never produces a message. I assume it has no effect.
tag_en is mapped to 'التصنيف', the same label as category_id. This is cosmetic, not a defect.

Every messages.* key used by the controllers (fetched, created, updated, deleted, login_success, logout_success, uploaded, quote_submitted) exists in both new messages files. I checked this and found no missing key.

second_author.subject: feat(personalities): add Personality entity for the story page's "faces" section
second_author.author: second author, fresh session, from the diff alone
second_author.defect: routes/admin.php changes four existing update routes (the groups at the hunks near lines 72, 89, 99 and 109) from Route::post('/{id}', 'update') to Route::put('/{id}', 'update'). It also registers the new personalities update as PUT, although UpdatePersonalityRequest/UpdatePersonalityAction accept an 'image' file upload. Two things follow. First, any existing client that updates those four resources with POST /{id} now gets 405 Method Not Allowed; the commit is about adding personalities and does not mention this. Second, PHP does not parse multipart/form-data bodies on PUT, so a genuine multipart PUT reaches Laravel with an empty input bag and no files. Because every update rule is nullable, the request passes validation, the DTO is all nulls, Arr::whereNotNull empties $data, and the endpoint returns 200 having changed nothing: the uploaded image and fields are silently dropped. Only clients that POST with _method=PUT (method spoofing) keep working. The POST /{id} routes were very likely that workaround, which this change removes.
required_context: routes/admin.php (full file, to identify which four resource groups were switched and whether their update requests take files)
app/Http/Requests/*/Update*Request.php::rules for those four resources (file/image fields)
the admin frontend's update calls for those resources (POST with or without _method, multipart or JSON); outside this repository
tests/Feature/* admin tests that postJson/post to /api/v1/admin/<resource>/{id}
config/cache.php 'default' and .env CACHE_STORE (Cache::tags throws on file/database stores)
database/seeders/PageContentSeeder.php::run (bulk insert vs per-row updateOrCreate) and the page_contents migration (whether a 'type' column exists)
app/Services/ImageService.php::store and ::delete (return shape ['path','url'] and failure behaviour)
app/Http/Requests/BaseFormRequest.php
app/Http/Resources/Concerns/ResolvesLocale.php::resolveLocale

inherited_member_dependence.why: The defect lives in routes/admin.php and in how PHP parses PUT bodies. The new controllers' inherited $this->success/created/deleted calls are not involved.

hedges: If every client already sends POST with _method=PUT, or sends JSON without files, the 405 and dropped-upload effects do not occur in practice. I cannot see the clients, which is why this is MODERATE rather than STRONG.
I assume Laravel's HTTP method parameter override is enabled (the framework default), so _method=PUT spoofing remains a working path.

Second, independent defect: the two new PageContentSeeder rows carry a 'type' => 'text' key that the neighbouring rows lack. If the seeder bulk-inserts the array, the rows have unequal column counts and the insert fails. If the table has no 'type' column, the rows fail or the key is silently discarded. I cannot tell without PageContentSeeder::run and the migration.

GetPersonalitiesAction and the create/update/delete actions call Cache::tags(['personalities']). This throws BadMethodCallException on non-tagging cache stores (file, database; Laravel 12's default is database). Presumably existing actions use the same pattern, but this is unverified.
UpdatePersonalityAction deletes the old image before storing the new one. If store() throws, the record keeps a path to a deleted file. This is minor and depends on ImageService.
UpdatePersonalityDTO maps an explicit is_active:null to false via has()+boolean(). A client sending null would deactivate the record. This is an edge case.
The cache key includes the locale although the cached value (raw models) is locale-independent. This is harmless redundancy, not a defect.
The tests assume the seeders run in setUp (5 seeded personalities). I cannot verify that.

key.subject: feat: menu PDF upload with permanent URL and QR code with logo
key.defect: TWO defects, either of which counts as detected. (a) upload() deletes the previously stored file and writes the new one to disk BEFORE the database write, with no transaction and no cleanup, so a failed Setting write leaves an orphaned file and the old file already gone. (b) payload() returns 'permanent_url' => route('menu.pdf'), the API domain, when the URL handed to users must be the frontend domain.
key.why_strong: Both are fixed by later real commits that name the mechanism. 04328a5 'fix: delete orphaned uploaded files when a DB write fails after upload' applies try/catch-and-delete across every upload Action. 2c2a7b4 'fix: menu PDF permanent_url uses frontend domain not API domain' replaces route('menu.pdf') with config('app.frontend_url').'/menu/pdf'.
key.visible_in_diff: PARTLY — the ordering of the file write and the DB write is visible; that no transaction wraps them, and that the URL is the wrong domain, both require knowledge the diff does not carry
expected_missing_context: the caller of upload(), to know whether a transaction surrounds it
key.bundle_relevant: PARTLY. The bundle flags the surrounding-transaction premise, which names defect (a)'s mechanism almost exactly. Nothing in it can reach defect (b), which is a configuration fact (X3).
